rationale: Scope of the real choice: F03 (uniform) and F04 (Sequence-only dissent) AGREE that REG3 applies uniformly at Sequence project_head/P7 and at resume/R7. The only live difference is bare stage::start for a NON-AWAITING /3 action: F03 applies REG3 there (refusing undeclared incoming discharge-only duties); F04 would let bare /3 non-awaiting admit them as /2 does and narrow only at the Sequence layer. Q1 (OD1/CSQ-016): neither policy is required; both are permitted. OD1 expressly delegates to the owner 'which local duty registry identities may be projected, including discharge-only incoming duties and await/R7 boundaries', so this is a genuine owner choice, not a forced one, provided current predicates are not silently weakened. CSQ-016 binds only /1 and /2; /3 is a new profile, so CSQ-016 is satisfied by either policy as long as the /2 start domain (canonical_boundary only for awaiting /2) and /1 are untouched, which both policies honor. I adopt the uniform choice. Explicit accepted domain loss: bare /3 non-awaiting discharge-only duties with no Statement::Liability must be source-declared via a /3 ExternalDutyDecl to be admitted; undeclared incoming duties are refused in both bare and Sequence domains. I accept that loss because /3 ships a declaration form precisely so incoming duty identity is source-authenticated, consistent with the principle (OD5/S048 in F04) that unauthenticated caller-supplied identity is not evidence; the F04 'benefit' of admitting undeclared incoming duties at bare /3 is in tension with that principle and produces an await-count-dependent seam under composition. Declared-vs-undeclared: declared duties are supported in both domains; undeclared refused in both. Awaiting-vs-non-awaiting: the uniform policy removes the await-count dependence entirely, which is the design goal. The /1 and /2 preservation prose (lines 5, 21) is sufficient AS A POLICY CONSTRAINT; I do NOT certify that admit.rs/admit_v3_tests.rs source actually achieves it. Q2 (H25): H25 is a boundary-domain decode/R7 guard on EMITTED Waiting outputs via emit_checked, not a liveness/progress/completion/resume guarantee, and it is silent on non-awaiting starts, which emit no continuation. The line-3 phrase 'a boundary admitted at /3 start remains resumable (H25)' overstates this; H25 does NOT by itself decide uniform non-awaiting bare-/3 admission, which is a separate explicit owner choice (correctly framed 'the owner chooses' in the RATIONALE). Because a security owner must not sign an overstated invariant, I adopt the uniform domain choice but REVISE the line-3 H25 sentence to the precise form in the amendment. Q3 (covered clauses): I adopt the domain policy in lines 3, 5, 19, 21; reject the Sequence-only alternative on the merits (await-count seam; unauthenticated-identity admission); preserve it and its revert-together condition as recorded non-operative dissent (line 23); and amend only the H25 sentence. This adopts no registry/parser/IR/schema/hash/callback/Meter/evaluator/SDK/compiler construction and leaves source security, runtime/effect eligibility, results, financial/composition coverage, native/proof/ledger/target/product obligations, B1 and PR310 open; the product stays permissionless with no user-program permission gate. Q4 (limits): no operative normative source is missing to decide this exact policy; downstream certification (REG3 predicate at lines 7-17, source/test results, execution eligibility) is separate and not performed. This remains a single independent vote; two agreeing votes plus root adoption and runtime-test selection are separate later steps.

dissent: Preserved Sequence-only alternative (F04 and F03 line 23): the admissibility-narrowing applied only at the Sequence admission layer, leaving bare /3 non-awaiting stage::start to admit undeclared incoming discharge-only duties as bare /2 does. Rejected on the merits here because it makes admissibility a function of successor await count, makes the lifted head's duty set non-uniform across invocations, and creates a silent domain seam in a serial chain where a non-awaiting head P could complete a discharge an otherwise-identical awaiting Q could not even project; it is nonetheless retained verbatim as recorded dissent, not relabelled complete.

Line-23 revert condition is preserved and binding on later process: if fresh whole source/design reviews and root adoption reject uniform bare-/3, root must revert the uniform condition in stage::start together with its ghost/mismatch uniform-start tests, and must not retain a narrowed Sequence-only target relabelled as the complete clause.

Residual precision concern carried forward even under adoption: the original line-3 'remains resumable (H25)' wording is an overstatement corrected by the amendment; reviewers must read H25 strictly as an emitted-Waiting decode/R7 boundary guard, never as a liveness, progress, completion or guaranteed-resume promise, and must treat non-awaiting bare-/3 REG3 admission as the owner's explicit policy choice rather than an H25 consequence.
